title: 신발 가게에서: 신어 봐도 돼요?
objective: You can ask to try shoes on and use -지만 (but).
summary: A customer asks for a size and tries shoes on.
setting: A shoe store. A customer is looking for white sneakers and tries on two sizes.

task.title: Use shoe-store Korean
task.line: Read the dialogue and word list, then do each exercise.

words.meaning: to put on, to wear (things on your feet: shoes, socks, stockings)

words.exampleMeaning: Go ahead and try them on.
These sneakers are light and comfortable.

words.meaning: I'll take this one (when you choose what to buy)
but (verb or adjective stem + 지만, joins two ideas that contrast)
words.exampleMeaning: These shoes are pretty, but they're uncomfortable.

dialogue.korean: 예쁘지만 색깔이 좀 어두워요. 흰색 있어요?
dialogue.meaning: They're pretty, but the color is a bit dark. Do you have white?
Yes, we do. What size do you wear?
Sure, go ahead and try them on.
I like the design, but they're a little small. Do you have 255?
Yes, just a moment. Here you are.

dialogue.korean: 딱 맞아요. 조금 무겁지만 편해요. 이걸로 주세요.
dialogue.meaning: They fit perfectly. They're a little heavy, but comfortable. I'll take these.

exercises: Fill in the blank with -지만, using the word in brackets: ① 이 운동화는 ____ 비싸요. (가볍다) ② 사이즈는 ____ 색깔이 어두워요. (맞다)
What do you say in Korean? ① You want to try the shoes on. ② You want to buy the pair in your hand.
Put the words in order to make one sentence: 작지만 / 이 구두는 / 예뻐요
Answer in English, based on the dialogue: ① What color does the customer want? ② Why doesn't the customer take size 250?
Choose the right word: ① 양말을 (신어요 / 맞아요). ② 이 사이즈가 딱 (맞아요 / 신어요).
answers: ① 신어 봐도 돼요? ② 이걸로 주세요.
① White ② They are a little small.
